title: Limit preservation for proper flat curves
statement: On schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of flat proper finitely presented morphisms $X\to T$ of algebraic spaces whose geometric fibres have dimension at most one [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Arrows in $\mathcal C(T)$ are $T$-isomorphisms and pullback is cartesian base change; arrows over $T'\to T$ are isomorphisms $X'\cong X\times_TT'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Algebraic spaces are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Flatness and local finite presentation for their morphisms are tested on etale scheme charts using [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper if it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion, finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). For every small directed inverse system $(T_i)$ of affine schemes with affine transition maps and limit $T$, the natural functor $\mathop{2\!\operatorname{colim}}_i\mathcal C(T_i)\to\mathcal C(T)$ is an equivalence. Explicitly, each family over $T$ descends to a stage; every isomorphism between the pullbacks of two stage families descends to a sufficiently late common stage; and two such isomorphisms equal over $T$ become equal at a sufficiently late common stage. Smallness is in [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Let $X\to T$ be an object of $\mathcal C(T)$. Apply [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] to its underlying finitely presented algebraic space: choose $i_0$, a finitely presented $X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$, and a $T$-isomorphism $X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T\cong X$. For $i\ge i_0$ write $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$. No flatness, properness, or fibre-dimension condition on this initial model is asserted. All morphisms in this application are morphisms of algebraic spaces, not just morphisms of schemes.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), expanded through the proof of lemma-spaces-limits.

proof.text: The limiting morphism is flat, so [lem-sfb-space-eventually-flat] gives $i_f\ge i_0$ such that every $X_j\to T_j$, $j\ge i_f$, is flat. Its finite-presentation hypothesis is exactly what the model in step 1 supplies; no Noetherian assumption is needed.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), expanded through the proof of lemma-spaces-limits.

proof.text: The limiting morphism is proper, so [lem-sfb-space-eventually-proper] gives $i_p\ge i_0$ such that every $X_j\to T_j$, $j\ge i_p$, is proper. The lemma applies before the initial model has been made separated or proper: finite presentation is its only extra hypothesis on that model.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), expanded through the proof of lemma-spaces-limits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-eventually-fibre-dimension] with $d=1$ to obtain $i_d\ge i_0$ such that every $X_j\to T_j$, $j\ge i_d$, has all geometric fibres of dimension at most one. Choose a common upper bound $j$ for $i_f,i_p,i_d$. The conclusions of steps 2--4 all hold at $j$, and finite presentation holds because the transition functors in [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] are base change on finitely presented objects. Thus $X_j\in\mathcal C(T_j)$, and its pullback is the original $X$. This proves essential surjectivity.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), expanded through the proof of lemma-spaces-limits.

proof.text: For two families at possibly different stages, choose a common stage $i$ and call their pullbacks $Y_i,Z_i$. They are still objects of $\mathcal C(T_i)$ by its stipulated cartesian pullback. Given a $T$-isomorphism $a:Y_i\times_{T_i}T\to Z_i\times_{T_i}T$, apply the morphism-descent clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category] to $a$ and separately to $a^{-1}$. At a common later stage $j$ both maps exist, say $a_j:Y_j\to Z_j$ and $b_j:Z_j\to Y_j$. Their composites pull back to the identity maps. Apply the eventual-equality clause of the same node to $b_ja_j$ and $\mathrm{id}_{Y_j}$, and to $a_jb_j$ and $\mathrm{id}_{Z_j}$. At a common later stage $k$ both equations hold. Hence $a_k$ and $b_k$ are inverse isomorphisms in $\mathcal C(T_k)$. This proves fullness without assuming that a descended morphism is automatically invertible.

source.place: Tag 0D55 (lemma-curves-limits), expanded through the proof of lemma-spaces-limits.

proof.text: If two stage isomorphisms have equal pullbacks over $T$, bring them to a common stage. The eventual-equality clause of [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category], applied to the underlying algebraic-space morphisms, makes them equal at a later stage. Isomorphisms have no extra data whose equality must be checked. Thus the functor is faithful. In the displayed filtered $2$-colimit, arrows are precisely stage isomorphisms modulo eventual equality; steps 5 and 6 make the arrow map bijective, and steps 1--4 give every object up to isomorphism. These are exactly the asserted equivalence and its three explicit clauses.

The four new unsplit nodes are true specializations of 07SK, 08K0, 08K1 and 0D4K to finitely presented spaces over affine bases. Their hypotheses hold: fp over an affine scheme gives qcqs and lfp, and the transition maps are affine. The 'every j >= i' clauses follow by base change (03MO, 04WP, 04NS). The geometric-fibre topological-dimension convention is equivalent to Stacks' relative dimension <= d through the decent-spaces lemma and field-extension invariance; empty fibres impose no condition. No new node restates a clause of the item; the only DAG hits are scheme analogues (lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper, lem-weil-pbc-descend-flat-finite-presentation, lem-trf-limit-fibre-dimension-bound), which are distinct, and same_as is []. Steps 1-4 follow the 0D1I route plus the 0D55 dimension bound, with a common index found by directedness and fp preserved by base change. Step 5 descends a and its inverse separately and imposes both composite identities by eventual equality. Step 6 is faithfulness. Edge cases checked: empty X, zero-dimensional fibres, automorphisms. No off-unit statement citations, no tool_uses and no SGA. Batch-5: the four citations of def-trf-algebraic-space point to a general definition of algebraic spaces that the item already cited on base, not part of the trace formula or Poincare duality or their proofs, so all four are accepted. Advisory only: fibre products of spaces are cited via the scheme node def-pc-fibre-product, and |X| of a space has no node; both are inherited from the item's own convention. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem properCurve_limit_preservation (I : Type u) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I] (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) [∀ i : I, IsAffine (D.obj (op i)).left] : (∀ X : ProperCurveFamily c.pt, ∃ (i : I) (Y : ProperCurveFamily (D.obj (op i))), Nonempty ((Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i)))).obj Y.presheafOver ≅ X.presheafOver)) ∧ (∀ (i j : I) (X : ProperCurveFamily (D.obj (op i))) (Y : ProperCurveFamily (D.obj (op j))) (a : (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i)))).obj X.presheafOver ≅ (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op j)))).obj Y.presheafOver), ∃ (k : I) (hik : i ≤ k) (hjk : j ≤ k) (b : (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE hik).op))).obj X.presheafOver ≅ (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE hjk).op))).obj Y.presheafOver), ProperCurveModuli.limitBaseChangeIso D c hik X.presheafOver ≪≫ (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op k)))).mapIso b ≪≫ (ProperCurveModuli.limitBaseChangeIso D c hjk Y.presheafOver).symm = a) ∧ (∀ (i : I) (X Y : ProperCurveFamily (D.obj (op i))) (a b : X.presheafOver ≅ Y.presheafOver), (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i)))).mapIso a = (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (c.π.app (op i)))).mapIso b → ∃ (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j), (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE hij).op))).mapIso a = (Over.pullback (yoneda.map (D.map (homOfLE hij).op))).mapIso b)
